meta.description: Select colormaps and qualitative palettes for scientific figures using perceptual-uniformity, color-vision-deficiency safety, and luminance-monotonicity criteria. Covers Crameri, viridis-family, Okabe-Ito, ColorBrewer, and jet/rainbow migration.
meta.execution_note: Executed all five archived inputs as regressions plus two genuinely new inputs. R and Python assertions reached PASS sentinels, Python exited 0, and all seven PNGs were manually opened plus pixel-checked. The shared R runtime currently exits 2816 during package teardown after successful output; a minimal ggplot2-only probe reproduces this outside the Skill, while a base-R probe exits 0. No Skill bytes or provider worktree files were modified.

scientific_integrity.detail: No result was fabricated; all reported centers, bounds, distances, mappings, masks, and plot properties were computed from saved synthetic fixtures or installed palette implementations.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill selects scientific figure encodings and makes no diagnosis, prescription, treatment recommendation, or participant-level inference.

methodological_ground.detail: Palette type matches data semantics in all seven outputs; quantitative bounds, CVD simulation, grayscale testing, and redundant encodings are correctly separated.

code_usability.detail: R and Python code parsed, executed all assertions, and emitted checked artifacts. Python and pixel checks exited 0. The post-success R exit 2816 is environment-wide and independently reproduces on loading ggplot2 alone, not a Skill code failure.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4, correctness 4, appropriateness 4. Sequential, diverging, cyclic, categorical, CVD, grayscale, migration, and >8-group boundaries are consistent and executable.

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 3, error reporting 3, recoverability 4. Version-introspection and design fallbacks are clear, although arbitrary non-finite data and custom reference points require agent judgment.

performance_context.note: Token cost 4, efficiency 4. SKILL.md is 252 lines; the guide routes rather than duplicates, and executable depth lives in examples/tests.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 4, consistency 4, feedback design 3, error prevention 4. The workflow is internally consistent and preventive; a compact result-report contract would further standardize responses.

human_usability.note: Discoverability 4, forgiveness 3. Natural prompts cover common requests; unusual nonzero midpoints and missing encodings are handled by generalization rather than explicit examples.

security.note: Credential safety 4, input validation 3, data safety 4. No secrets, shell interpolation, network calls, destructive operations, or data retention are present.

maintainability.note: Modularity 4, modifiability 4, testability 4. Concise guide, two self-contained examples, and focused R/Python contract tests cleanly separate responsibilities.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision 4, progressive disclosure 4, composability 3, idempotency 4, escape hatches 3. The trigger is precise and >8/>20 group limits are explicit; response integration points remain informal.

inputs.label: Named Okabe-Ito mapping for seven cell types plus unassigned
inputs.note: The fixed named mapping stayed byte-for-byte stable after T cells were removed. Unassigned used #BBBBBB plus a distinct cross marker; R CIELAB minima after deutan/protan/tritan transforms were 14.93/20.71/16.17.

assertions.text: Every category is assigned through a named mapping and Unassigned is light grey
assertions.note: Seven chromatic names plus Unassigned=#BBBBBB were present.

assertions.text: Removing T cells does not recolor any remaining category
assertions.note: The full and subset ggplot_build mappings were identical for all shared levels.

assertions.text: All three CVD simulations produce finite positive minimum pairwise distances
assertions.note: R minima were 14.93, 20.71, and 16.17; Python independently returned 14.17, 13.96, and 10.97 in CAM02-UCS.

assertions.text: A redundant non-color encoding distinguishes the reserve class
assertions.note: Unassigned uses marker 4 while chromatic categories use marker 16.

assertions.text: The full and subset plots render non-blank with readable legends
assertions.note: Manual visual inspection confirmed stable colors, the grey cross class, and complete legends.

assertions.note: The 101-color custom ramp's 51st color was #FFFFFF.

inputs.note: The output generalized the diverging principle to a scientifically meaningful reference of 0.5, masked 48 missing cells, and encoded them as #BBBBBB. The reference maps exactly to 0.5 in the norm.

assertions.note: TwoSlopeNorm(vcenter=0.5) returns 0.5 at the reference.

assertions.text: Missing values are not silently mapped to a quantitative color
assertions.note: The masked array uses cmap bad color #BBBBBB.

assertions.text: All missing cells are preserved as missing
assertions.note: The mask count is 48, matching the synthetic missing block.

assertions.text: The two arms use explicit symmetric conceptual bounds around the reference
assertions.note: The fraction limits are 0 and 1 around reference 0.5.

assertions.text: The reference and missing regions are visually distinct
assertions.note: Manual inspection shows a white reference block and a separate grey missing block.

final.grade_note: All Production Ready floors pass: static 93>=80, execution 94.9>=85, Layer 1 average 38.3>=32, Layer 2 average 56.6>=48, assertions 35/35=100%, no veto, and no open P0.

key_strengths: The fixed guidance is internally consistent across sequential, diverging, cyclic, and categorical use cases, including measured built-in centres and data-derived symmetric limits.
CVD and grayscale checks now execute in both R and Python and report finite distances while explicitly avoiding a false universal accessibility cutoff.
Named categorical mappings remain stable across subsets, reserve grey is explicit, and redundant shape/facet strategies are used when hue cannot safely carry identity.
Both shipped examples are self-contained, match the prose, and are backed by focused cross-language contract tests.

recommendations.title: Add a compact palette-audit response contract
recommendations.problem: The Skill specifies the computations but not a single standard response shape for reporting the chosen type, limits, midpoint, grayscale result, CVD minima, redundant encoding, and visual-inspection outcome.
recommendations.root_cause: Feedback expectations are distributed across several sections rather than summarized as an output checklist.
recommendations.fix: Add a short final-response checklist with palette name/type, normalization and bounds, CVD minima, luminance verdict, redundant encoding, and visual inspection status.

recommendations.title: Show arbitrary reference points and missing values
recommendations.problem: The nonzero-reference case succeeded, but the Skill only demonstrates midpoint zero and does not explicitly show how to mask missing values with a non-quantitative bad color.
recommendations.root_cause: Examples center on signed LFC/z-score data and assume finite numeric matrices.
recommendations.fix: Add one compact Python or R note: set the diverging midpoint to the scientific reference value, mask non-finite cells, and assign missing values a separate neutral color such as #BBBBBB.
